audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Judges / Shoftim Abimelech kingship, Jotham fable, Shechem conflict, and Thebez death narrative, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Abimelech's Shechem appeal, hired reckless men, slaughter of seventy brothers, Jotham's tree fable, three-year rule, evil spirit, Gaal revolt, Shechem massacre, tower burning, Thebez millstone death, armor-bearer suicide request, and bloodguilt return theology.

verses.restored: Abimelech son of Jerubbaal went to Shechem, to brothers of his mother, and spoke to them and to all clan of house of his mother's father, saying,

familiar.text: And Abimelech the son of Jerubbaal went to Shechem unto his mother’s brethren, and communed with them, and with all the family of the house of his mother’s father, saying,

modern.text: Now Abimelech son of Jerubbaal went to his mother’s brothers at Shechem and said to them and to all the clan of his mother,

original.text: וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ אֲבִימֶ֤לֶךְ בֶּן יְרֻבַּ֨עַל֙ שְׁכֶ֔מָה אֶל אֲחֵ֖י אִמּ֑וֹ וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם וְאֶל כָּל מִשְׁפַּ֛חַת בֵּית אֲבִ֥י אִמּ֖וֹ לֵאמֹֽר

verses.restored: Speak, please, in ears of all lords of Shechem: Which is better for you, that seventy men rule over you, all sons of Jerubbaal, or that one man rule over you? Remember that I am your bone and your flesh.

familiar.text: Speak, I pray you, in the ears of all the men of Shechem, Whether is better for you, either that all the sons of Jerubbaal, which are threescore and ten persons, reign over you, or that one reign over you? remember also that I am your bone and your flesh.

modern.text: “Please ask all the leaders of Shechem, ‘Is it better for you that seventy men, all the sons of Jerubbaal, rule over you, or just one man?’ Remember that I am your own flesh and blood.”

original.text: דַּבְּרוּ נָ֞א בְּאָזְנֵ֨י כָל בַּעֲלֵ֣י שְׁכֶם֮ מַה טּ֣וֹב לָכֶם֒ הַמְשֹׁ֨ל בָּכֶ֜ם שִׁבְעִ֣ים אִ֗ישׁ כֹּ֚ל בְּנֵ֣י יְרֻבַּ֔עַל אִם מְשֹׁ֥ל בָּכֶ֖ם אִ֣ישׁ אֶחָ֑ד וּזְכַרְתֶּ֕ם כִּֽי עַצְמֵכֶם וּבְשַׂרְכֶ֖ם אָנִֽי

verses.restored: Brothers of his mother spoke about him in ears of all lords of Shechem all these words, and their heart inclined after Abimelech, for they said, He is our brother.

familiar.text: And his mother’s brethren spake of him in the ears of all the men of Shechem all these words: and their hearts inclined to follow Abimelech; for they said, He is our brother.

modern.text: And when his mother’s brothers spoke all these words about him in the presence of all the leaders of Shechem, their hearts were inclined to follow Abimelech, for they said, “He is our brother.”

original.text: וַיְדַבְּר֨וּ אֲחֵֽי אִמּ֜וֹ עָלָ֗יו בְּאָזְנֵי֙ כָּל בַּעֲלֵ֣י שְׁכֶ֔ם אֵ֥ת כָּל הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַיֵּ֤ט לִבָּם֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י אֲבִימֶ֔לֶךְ כִּ֥י אָמְר֖וּ אָחִ֥ינוּ הֽוּא

verses.restored: They gave him seventy pieces of silver from house of Baal-berith; with them Abimelech hired empty and reckless men, and they went after him.

familiar.text: And they gave him threescore and ten pieces of silver out of the house of Baalberith, wherewith Abimelech hired vain and light persons, which followed him.

modern.text: So they gave him seventy shekels of silver from the temple of Baal-berith, with which Abimelech hired some worthless and reckless men to follow him.

original.text: וַיִּתְּנוּ לוֹ֙ שִׁבְעִ֣ים כֶּ֔סֶף מִבֵּ֖יתּ בַ֣עַל בְּרִ֑ית וַיִּשְׂכֹּ֨ר בָּהֶ֜ם אֲבִימֶ֗לֶךְ אֲנָשִׁ֤ים רֵיקִים֙ וּפֹ֣חֲזִ֔ים וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ אַחֲרָֽיו

verses.restored: He came to house of his father at Ophrah and killed his brothers, sons of Jerubbaal, seventy men upon one stone. But Jotham youngest son of Jerubbaal remained, for he hid.

familiar.text: And he went unto his father’s house at Ophrah, and slew his brethren the sons of Jerubbaal, being threescore and ten persons, upon one stone: notwithstanding yet Jotham the youngest son of Jerubbaal was left; for he hid himself.

modern.text: He went to his father’s house in Ophrah, and on one stone murdered his seventy brothers, the sons of Jerubbaal. But Jotham, the youngest son of Jerubbaal, survived, because he hid himself.

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֤א בֵית אָבִיו֙ עָפְרָ֔תָה וַֽיַּהֲרֹ֞ג אֶת אֶחָ֧יו בְּנֵֽי יְרֻבַּ֛עַל שִׁבְּעִ֥ים אִ֖ישׁ עַל אֶ֣בֶן אֶחָ֑ת וַיִּוָּתֵ֞ר יוֹתָ֧ם בֶּן יְרֻבַּ֛עַל הַקָּטֹ֖ן כִּ֥י נֶחְבָּֽא

verses.restored: All lords of Shechem and all Beth-millo gathered and went and made Abimelech king by oak of pillar that was in Shechem.

familiar.text: And all the men of Shechem gathered together, and all the house of Millo, and went, and made Abimelech king, by the plain of the pillar that was in Shechem.

modern.text: Then all the leaders of Shechem and Beth-millo gathered beside the oak at the pillar in Shechem and proceeded to make Abimelech their king. Jotham’s Parable

original.text: וַיֵּאָ֨סְפ֜וּ כָּל בַּעֲלֵ֤י שְׁכֶם֙ וְכָל בֵּ֣ית מִלּ֔וֹא וַיֵּ֣לְכ֔וּ וַיַּמְלִ֥יכוּ אֶת אֲבִימֶ֖לֶךְ לְמֶ֑לֶךְ עִם אֵל֥וֹן מֻצָּ֖ב אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּשְׁכֶֽם

verses.restored: They told Jotham, and he went and stood at top of Mount Gerizim and lifted his voice and called and said to them: Listen to me, lords of Shechem, so Divine may listen to you.

familiar.text: And when they told it to Jotham, he went and stood in the top of mount Gerizim, and lifted up his voice, and cried, and said unto them, Hearken unto me, ye men of Shechem, that God may hearken unto you.

modern.text: When this was reported to Jotham, he climbed to the top of Mount Gerizim, raised his voice, and cried out: “Listen to me, O leaders of Shechem, and may God listen to you.

original.text: וַיַּגִּ֣דוּ לְיוֹתָ֗ם וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ֙ וַֽיַּעֲמֹד֙ בְּרֹ֣אשׁ הַר גְּרִזִ֔ים וַיִּשָּׂ֥א קוֹל֖וֹ וַיִּקְרָ֑א וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֗ם שִׁמְע֤וּ אֵלַי֙ בַּעֲלֵ֣י שְׁכֶ֔ם וְיִשְׁמַ֥ע אֲלֵיכֶ֖ם אֱלֹהִֽים

verses.restored: The trees surely went to anoint over themselves a king. They said to olive tree, Reign over us.

familiar.text: The trees went forth on a time to anoint a king over them; and they said unto the olive tree, Reign thou over us.

modern.text: One day the trees set out to anoint a king for themselves. They said to the olive tree, ‘Reign over us.’

original.text: הָל֤וֹךְ הָֽלְכוּ֙ הָעֵצִ֔ים לִמְשֹׁ֥חַ עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם מֶ֑לֶךְ וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ לַזַּ֖יִת מלוכה עָלֵֽינוּ

verses.restored: Olive tree said to them, Shall I cease my fatness/oil, by which Divine and men are honored, and go sway over trees?

familiar.text: But the olive tree said unto them, Should I leave my fatness, wherewith by me they honour God and man, and go to be promoted over the trees?

modern.text: But the olive tree replied, ‘Should I stop giving my oil that honors both God and man, to hold sway over the trees?’

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ הַזַּ֔יִת הֶחֳדַ֨לְתִּי֙ אֶת דִּשְׁנִ֔י אֲשֶׁר בִּ֛י יְכַבְּד֥וּ אֱלֹהִ֖ים וַאֲנָשִׁ֑ים וְהָ֣לַכְתִּ֔י לָנ֖וּעַ עַל הָעֵצִֽים

verses.restored: The trees said to fig tree, You come, reign over us.

familiar.text: And the trees said to the fig tree, Come thou, and reign over us.

modern.text: Then the trees said to the fig tree, ‘Come and reign over us.’

original.text: וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ הָעֵצִ֖ים לַתְּאֵנָ֑ה לְכִי אַ֖תְּ מָלְכִ֥י עָלֵֽינוּ

verses.restored: Fig tree said to them, Shall I cease my sweetness and my good fruit and go sway over trees?

familiar.text: But the fig tree said unto them, Should I forsake my sweetness, and my good fruit, and go to be promoted over the trees?

modern.text: But the fig tree replied, ‘Should I stop giving my sweetness and my good fruit, to hold sway over the trees?’

original.text: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ הַתְּאֵנָ֔ה הֶחֳדַ֨לְתִּי֙ אֶת מָתְקִ֔י וְאֶת תְּנוּבָתִ֖י הַטּוֹבָ֑ה וְהָ֣לַכְתִּ֔י לָנ֖וּעַ עַל הָעֵצִֽים

verses.restored: The trees said to vine, You come, reign over us.

familiar.text: Then said the trees unto the vine, Come thou, and reign over us.

modern.text: Then the trees said to the grapevine, ‘Come and reign over us.’

original.text: וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ הָעֵצִ֖ים לַגָּ֑פֶן לְכִי אַ֖תְּ מלוכי עָלֵֽינוּ

verses.restored: Vine said to them, Shall I cease my new wine, which gladdens Divine and men, and go sway over trees?

familiar.text: And the vine said unto them, Should I leave my wine, which cheereth God and man, and go to be promoted over the trees?

modern.text: But the grapevine replied, ‘Should I stop giving my wine that cheers both God and man, to hold sway over the trees?’

original.text: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ הַגֶּ֔פֶן הֶחֳדַ֨לְתִּי֙ אֶת תִּ֣ירוֹשִׁ֔י הַֽמְשַׂמֵּ֥חַ אֱלֹהִ֖ים וַאֲנָשִׁ֑ים וְהָ֣לַכְתִּ֔י לָנ֖וּעַ עַל הָעֵצִֽים

verses.restored: All trees said to bramble, You come, reign over us.

familiar.text: Then said all the trees unto the bramble, Come thou, and reign over us.

modern.text: Finally all the trees said to the thornbush, ‘Come and reign over us.’

original.text: וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ כָל הָעֵצִ֖ים אֶל הָאָטָ֑ד לֵ֥ךְ אַתָּ֖ה מְלָךְ עָלֵֽינוּ

verses.restored: Bramble said to trees, If in faithfulness you are anointing me king over you, come take refuge in my shade; but if not, let fire go out from bramble and consume cedars of Lebanon.

familiar.text: And the bramble said unto the trees, If in truth ye anoint me king over you, then come and put your trust in my shadow: and if not, let fire come out of the bramble, and devour the cedars of Lebanon.

modern.text: But the thornbush replied, ‘If you really are anointing me as king over you, come and find refuge in my shade. But if not, may fire come out of the thornbush and consume the cedars of Lebanon.’

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הָאָטָד֮ אֶל הָעֵצִים֒ אִ֡ם בֶּאֱמֶ֣ת אַתֶּם֩ מֹשְׁחִ֨ים אֹתִ֤י לְמֶ֨לֶךְ֙ עֲלֵיכֶ֔ם בֹּ֖אוּ חֲס֣וּ בְצִלִּ֑י וְאִם אַ֕יִן תֵּ֤צֵא אֵשׁ֙ מִן הָ֣אָטָ֔ד וְתֹאכַ֖ל אֶת אַרְזֵ֥י הַלְּבָנֽוֹן

verses.restored: Now therefore, if in faithfulness and wholeness you acted when you made Abimelech king, and if you did good with Jerubbaal and his house, and if according to deserving of his hands you did to him—

familiar.text: Now therefore, if ye have done truly and sincerely, in that ye have made Abimelech king, and if ye have dealt well with Jerubbaal and his house, and have done unto him according to the deserving of his hands;

modern.text: Now if you have acted faithfully and honestly in making Abimelech king, if you have done well by Jerubbaal and his family, and if you have done to him as he deserves—

original.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה אִם בֶּאֱמֶ֤ת וּבְתָמִים֙ עֲשִׂיתֶ֔ם וַתַּמְלִ֖יכוּ אֶת אֲבִימֶ֑לֶךְ וְאִם טוֹבָ֤ה עֲשִׂיתֶם֙ עִם יְרֻבַּ֣עַל וְעִם בֵּית֔וֹ וְאִם כִּגְמ֥וּל יָדָ֖יו עֲשִׂ֥יתֶם לֽוֹ

verses.restored: for my father fought for you and cast his soul/life in front and rescued you from hand of Midian,

familiar.text: (For my father fought for you, and adventured his life far, and delivered you out of the hand of Midian:

modern.text: for my father fought for you and risked his life to deliver you from the hand of Midian,

original.text: אֲשֶׁר נִלְחַ֥ם אָבִ֖י עֲלֵיכֶ֑ם וַיַּשְׁלֵ֤ךְ אֶת נַפְשׁוֹ֙ מִנֶּ֔גֶד וַיַּצֵּ֥ל אֶתְכֶ֖ם מִיַּ֥ד מִדְיָֽן

verses.restored: but you rose against house of my father today and killed his sons, seventy men upon one stone, and made Abimelech, son of his slave woman, king over lords of Shechem because he is your brother—

familiar.text: And ye are risen up against my father’s house this day, and have slain his sons, threescore and ten persons, upon one stone, and have made Abimelech, the son of his maidservant, king over the men of Shechem, because he is your brother;)

modern.text: but you have risen up against my father’s house this day and killed his seventy sons on a single stone, and you have made Abimelech, the son of his maidservant, king over the leaders of Shechem because he is your brother—

original.text: וְאַתֶּ֞ם קַמְתֶּ֨ם עַל בֵּ֤ית אָבִי֙ הַיּ֔וֹם וַתַּהַרְג֧וּ אֶת בָּנָ֛יו שִׁבְעִ֥ים אִ֖ישׁ עַל אֶ֣בֶן אֶחָ֑ת וַתַּמְלִ֜יכוּ אֶת אֲבִימֶ֤לֶךְ בֶּן אֲמָתוֹ֙ עַל בַּעֲלֵ֣י שְׁכֶ֔ם כִּ֥י אֲחִיכֶ֖ם הֽוּא

verses.restored: if in faithfulness and wholeness you acted with Jerubbaal and his house this day, rejoice in Abimelech, and let him also rejoice in you.

familiar.text: If ye then have dealt truly and sincerely with Jerubbaal and with his house this day, then rejoice ye in Abimelech, and let him also rejoice in you:

modern.text: if you have acted faithfully and honestly toward Jerubbaal and his house this day, then may you rejoice in Abimelech, and he in you.

original.text: וְאִם בֶּאֱמֶ֨ת וּבְתָמִ֧ים עֲשִׂיתֶ֛ם עִם יְרֻבַּ֥עַל וְעִם בֵּית֖וֹ הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה שִׂמְחוּ֙ בַּאֲבִימֶ֔לֶךְ וְיִשְׂמַ֥ח גַּם ה֖וּא בָּכֶֽם

verses.restored: But if not, let fire go out from Abimelech and consume lords of Shechem and Beth-millo, and let fire go out from lords of Shechem and Beth-millo and consume Abimelech.

familiar.text: But if not, let fire come out from Abimelech, and devour the men of Shechem, and the house of Millo; and let fire come out from the men of Shechem, and from the house of Millo, and devour Abimelech.

modern.text: But if not, may fire come from Abimelech and consume the leaders of Shechem and Beth-millo, and may fire come from the leaders of Shechem and Beth-millo and consume Abimelech.”

original.text: וְאִם אַ֕יִן תֵּ֤צֵא אֵשׁ֙ מֵאֲבִימֶ֔לֶךְ וְתֹאכַ֛ל אֶת בַּעֲלֵ֥י שְׁכֶ֖ם וְאֶת בֵּ֣ית מִלּ֑וֹא וְתֵצֵ֨א אֵ֜שׁ מִבַּעֲלֵ֤י שְׁכֶם֙ וּמִבֵּ֣ית מִלּ֔וֹא וְתֹאכַ֖ל אֶת אֲבִימֶֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: Jotham fled and escaped and went to Beer; he dwelt there away from Abimelech his brother.

familiar.text: And Jotham ran away, and fled, and went to Beer, and dwelt there, for fear of Abimelech his brother.

modern.text: Then Jotham ran away, escaping to Beer, and he lived there for fear of his brother Abimelech. Gaal Conspires with the Shechemites

original.text: וַיָּ֣נָס יוֹתָ֔ם וַיִּבְרַ֖ח וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ בְּאֵ֑רָה וַיֵּ֣שֶׁב שָׁ֔ם מִפְּנֵ֖י אֲבִימֶ֥לֶךְ אָחִֽיו

verses.restored: Abimelech ruled over Israel three years.

familiar.text: When Abimelech had reigned three years over Israel,

modern.text: After Abimelech had reigned over Israel for three years,

original.text: וַיָּ֧שַׂר אֲבִימֶ֛לֶךְ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל שָׁלֹ֥שׁ שָׁנִֽים

verses.restored: Divine sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and lords of Shechem, and lords of Shechem acted treacherously against Abimelech,

familiar.text: Then God sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and the men of Shechem; and the men of Shechem dealt treacherously with Abimelech:

modern.text: God sent a spirit of animosity between Abimelech and the leaders of Shechem and caused them to treat Abimelech deceitfully,

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח אֱלֹהִים֙ ר֣וּחַ רָעָ֔ה בֵּ֣ין אֲבִימֶ֔לֶךְ וּבֵ֖ין בַּעֲלֵ֣י שְׁכֶ֑ם וַיִּבְגְּד֥וּ בַעֲלֵי שְׁכֶ֖ם בַּאֲבִימֶֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: so violence done to seventy sons of Jerubbaal might come, and their blood be placed upon Abimelech their brother who killed them and upon lords of Shechem who strengthened his hands to kill his brothers.

familiar.text: That the cruelty done to the threescore and ten sons of Jerubbaal might come, and their blood be laid upon Abimelech their brother, which slew them; and upon the men of Shechem, which aided him in the killing of his brethren.

modern.text: in order that the crime against the seventy sons of Jerubbaal might come to justice and their blood be avenged on their brother Abimelech and on the leaders of Shechem, who had helped him murder his brothers.

original.text: לָב֕וֹא חֲמַ֖ס שִׁבְעִ֣ים בְּנֵֽי יְרֻבָּ֑עַל וְדָמָ֗ם לָשׂ֞וּם עַל אֲבִימֶ֤לֶךְ אֲחִיהֶם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָרַ֣ג אוֹתָ֔ם וְעַל֙ בַּעֲלֵ֣י שְׁכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁר חִזְּק֥וּ אֶת יָדָ֖יו לַהֲרֹ֥ג אֶת אֶחָֽיו

verses.restored: Lords of Shechem set ambushers against him on tops of mountains, and they robbed everyone who passed by them on road; it was told to Abimelech.

familiar.text: And the men of Shechem set liers in wait for him in the top of the mountains, and they robbed all that came along that way by them: and it was told Abimelech.

modern.text: The leaders of Shechem set up an ambush against Abimelech on the hilltops, and they robbed all who passed by them on the road. So this was reported to Abimelech.

original.text: וַיָּשִׂ֣ימוּ לוֹ֩ בַעֲלֵ֨י שְׁכֶ֜ם מְאָרְבִ֗ים עַ֚ל רָאשֵׁ֣י הֶהָרִ֔ים וַיִּגְזְל֗וּ אֵ֛ת כָּל אֲשֶׁר יַעֲבֹ֥ר עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם בַּדָּ֑רֶךְ וַיֻּגַּ֖ד לַאֲבִימֶֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: Gaal son of Ebed came with his brothers and crossed into Shechem, and lords of Shechem trusted in him.

familiar.text: And Gaal the son of Ebed came with his brethren, and went over to Shechem: and the men of Shechem put their confidence in him.

modern.text: Meanwhile, Gaal son of Ebed came with his brothers and crossed into Shechem, and the leaders of Shechem put their confidence in him.

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֞א גַּ֤עַל בֶּן עֶ֨בֶד֙ וְאֶחָ֔יו וַיַּעַבְר֖וּ בִּשְׁכֶ֑ם וַיִּבְטְחוּ ב֖וֹ בַּעֲלֵ֥י שְׁכֶֽם

verses.restored: They went out to field, gathered their vineyards, trod grapes, and made praise-songs/revelry; they came into house of their god, ate and drank, and cursed Abimelech.

familiar.text: And they went out into the fields, and gathered their vineyards, and trode the grapes, and made merry, and went into the house of their god, and did eat and drink, and cursed Abimelech.

modern.text: And after they had gone out into the fields, gathered grapes from their vineyards, and trodden them, they held a festival and went into the house of their god; and as they ate and drank, they cursed Abimelech.

original.text: וַיֵּצְא֨וּ הַשָּׂדֶ֜ה וַֽיִּבְצְר֤וּ אֶת כַּרְמֵיהֶם֙ וַֽיִּדְרְכ֔וּ וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֖וּ הִלּוּלִ֑ים וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ בֵּ֣ית אֱֽלֹֽהֵיהֶ֔ם וַיֹּֽאכְלוּ֙ וַיִּשְׁתּ֔וּ וַֽיְקַלְל֖וּ אֶת אֲבִימֶֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: Gaal son of Ebed said, Who is Abimelech, and who is Shechem, that we should serve him? Is he not son of Jerubbaal, and Zebul his officer? Serve men of Hamor father of Shechem; why should we serve him?

familiar.text: And Gaal the son of Ebed said, Who is Abimelech, and who is Shechem, that we should serve him? is not he the son of Jerubbaal? and Zebul his officer? serve the men of Hamor the father of Shechem: for why should we serve him?

modern.text: Then Gaal son of Ebed said, “Who is Abimelech, and who is Shechem, that we should serve him? Is he not the son of Jerubbaal, and is not Zebul his officer? You are to serve the men of Hamor, the father of Shechem. Why should we serve Abimelech?

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר גַּ֣עַל בֶּן עֶ֗בֶד מִֽי אֲבִימֶ֤לֶךְ וּמִֽי שְׁכֶם֙ כִּ֣י נַעַבְדֶ֔נּוּ הֲלֹ֥א בֶן יְרֻבַּ֖עַל וּזְבֻ֣ל פְּקִיד֑וֹ עִבְד֗וּ אֶת אַנְשֵׁ֤י חֲמוֹר֙ אֲבִ֣י שְׁכֶ֔ם וּמַדּ֖וּעַ נַעַבְדֶ֥נּוּ אֲנָֽחְנוּ

verses.restored: Would that this people were in my hand! Then I would remove Abimelech. He said to Abimelech, Increase your army and come out.

familiar.text: And would to God this people were under my hand! then would I remove Abimelech. And he said to Abimelech, Increase thine army, and come out.

modern.text: If only this people were under my authority, I would remove Abimelech; I would say to him, ‘Muster your army and come out!’” The Fall of Shechem

original.text: וּמִ֨י יִתֵּ֜ן אֶת הָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ בְּיָדִ֔י וְאָסִ֖ירָה אֶת אֲבִימֶ֑לֶךְ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ לַאֲבִימֶ֔לֶךְ רַבֶּ֥ה צְבָאֲךָ֖ וָצֵֽאָה

verses.restored: Zebul ruler of city heard words of Gaal son of Ebed, and his anger burned.

familiar.text: And when Zebul the ruler of the city heard the words of Gaal the son of Ebed, his anger was kindled.

modern.text: When Zebul the governor of the city heard the words of Gaal son of Ebed, he burned with anger.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֗ע זְבֻל֙ שַׂר הָעִ֔יר אֶת דִּבְרֵ֖י גַּ֣עַל בֶּן עָ֑בֶד וַיִּ֖חַר אַפּֽוֹ

verses.restored: He sent messengers to Abimelech in deceit/Tormah, saying, Look, Gaal son of Ebed and his brothers are coming to Shechem, and look, they are stirring city against you.

familiar.text: And he sent messengers unto Abimelech privily, saying, Behold, Gaal the son of Ebed and his brethren be come to Shechem; and, behold, they fortify the city against thee.

modern.text: So he covertly sent messengers to Abimelech to say, “Look, Gaal son of Ebed and his brothers have come to Shechem and are stirring up the city against you.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֧ח מַלְאָכִ֛ים אֶל אֲבִימֶ֖לֶךְ בְּתָרְמָ֣ה לֵאמֹ֑ר הִנֵּה֩ גַ֨עַל בֶּן עֶ֤בֶד וְאֶחָיו֙ בָּאִ֣ים שְׁכֶ֔מָה וְהִנָּ֛ם צָרִ֥ים אֶת הָעִ֖יר עָלֶֽיךָ

verses.restored: Now rise by night, you and people with you, and lie in ambush in field.

familiar.text: Now therefore up by night, thou and the people that is with thee, and lie in wait in the field:

modern.text: Now then, tonight you and the people with you are to come and lie in wait in the fields.

original.text: וְעַתָּה֙ ק֣וּם לַ֔יְלָה אַתָּ֖ה וְהָעָ֣ם אֲשֶׁר אִתָּ֑ךְ וֶאֱרֹ֖ב בַּשָּׂדֶֽה

verses.restored: It shall be in morning, when sun rises, rise early and rush upon city. Look, when he and people with him come out to you, you shall do to him as your hand finds.

familiar.text: And it shall be, that in the morning, as soon as the sun is up, thou shalt rise early, and set upon the city: and, behold, when he and the people that is with him come out against thee, then mayest thou do to them as thou shalt find occasion.

modern.text: And in the morning at sunrise, get up and advance against the city. When Gaal and his men come out against you, do to them whatever you are able.”

original.text: וְהָיָ֤ה בַבֹּ֨קֶר֙ כִּזְרֹ֣חַ הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ תַּשְׁכִּ֖ים וּפָשַׁטְתָּ֣ עַל הָעִ֑יר וְהִנֵּה ה֞וּא וְהָעָ֤ם אֲשֶׁר אִתּוֹ֙ יֹצְאִ֣ים אֵלֶ֔יךָ וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ לּ֔וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר תִּמְצָ֥א יָדֶֽךָ

verses.restored: Abimelech and all people with him rose by night and lay in ambush against Shechem, four companies.

familiar.text: And Abimelech rose up, and all the people that were with him, by night, and they laid wait against Shechem in four companies.

modern.text: So Abimelech and all his troops set out by night and lay in wait against Shechem in four companies.

original.text: וַיָּ֧קָם אֲבִימֶ֛לֶךְ וְכָל הָעָ֥ם אֲשֶׁר עִמּ֖וֹ לָ֑יְלָה וַיֶּאֶרְב֣וּ עַל שְׁכֶ֔ם אַרְבָּעָ֖ה רָאשִֽׁים

verses.restored: Gaal son of Ebed went out and stood at entrance of gate of city, and Abimelech and people with him rose from ambush.

familiar.text: And Gaal the son of Ebed went out, and stood in the entering of the gate of the city: and Abimelech rose up, and the people that were with him, from lying in wait.

modern.text: Now Gaal son of Ebed went out and stood at the entrance of the city gate just as Abimelech and his men came out from their hiding places.

original.text: וַיֵּצֵא֙ גַּ֣עַל בֶּן עֶ֔בֶד וַיַּעֲמֹ֕ד פֶּ֖תַח שַׁ֣עַר הָעִ֑יר וַיָּ֧קָם אֲבִימֶ֛לֶךְ וְהָעָ֥ם אֲשֶׁר אִתּ֖וֹ מִן הַמַּאְרָֽב

verses.restored: Gaal saw people and said to Zebul, Look, people are coming down from tops of mountains. Zebul said to him, Shadow of mountains you are seeing as men.

familiar.text: And when Gaal saw the people, he said to Zebul, Behold, there come people down from the top of the mountains. And Zebul said unto him, Thou seest the shadow of the mountains as if they were men.

modern.text: When Gaal saw the people, he said to Zebul, “Look, people are coming down from the mountains!” But Zebul replied, “The shadows of the mountains look like men to you.”

original.text: וַיַּרְא גַּעַל֮ אֶת הָעָם֒ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶל זְבֻ֔ל הִנֵּה עָ֣ם יוֹרֵ֔ד מֵרָאשֵׁ֖י הֶהָרִ֑ים וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ זְבֻ֔ל אֵ֣ת צֵ֧ל הֶהָרִ֛ים אַתָּ֥ה רֹאֶ֖ה כָּאֲנָשִֽׁים

verses.restored: Gaal spoke again and said, Look, people are coming down from navel of land, and one company is coming from way of Diviners' Oak.

familiar.text: And Gaal spake again and said, See there come people down by the middle of the land, and another company come along by the plain of Meonenim.

modern.text: Then Gaal spoke up again, “Look, people are coming down from the center of the land, and one company is coming by way of the Diviners’ Oak. ”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨סֶף ע֣וֹד גַּעַל֮ לְדַבֵּר֒ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הִנֵּה עָם֙ יֽוֹרְדִ֔ים מֵעִ֖ם טַבּ֣וּר הָאָ֑רֶץ וְרֹאשׁ אֶחָ֣ד בָּ֔א מִדֶּ֖רֶךְ אֵל֥וֹן מְעוֹנְנִֽים

verses.restored: Zebul said to him, Where now is your mouth, you who said, Who is Abimelech that we should serve him? Is this not people you despised? Go out now and fight with them.

familiar.text: Then said Zebul unto him, Where is now thy mouth, wherewith thou saidst, Who is Abimelech, that we should serve him? is not this the people that thou hast despised? go out, I pray now, and fight with them.

modern.text: “Where is your gloating now?” Zebul replied. “You said, ‘Who is Abimelech that we should serve him?’ Are these not the people you ridiculed? Go out now and fight them!”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֜יו זְבֻ֗ל אַיֵּ֨ה אֵפ֥וֹא פִ֨יךָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תֹּאמַ֔ר מִ֥י אֲבִימֶ֖לֶךְ כִּ֣י נַעַבְדֶ֑נּוּ הֲלֹ֨א זֶ֤ה הָעָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר מָאַ֣סְתָּה בּ֔וֹ צֵא נָ֥א עַתָּ֖ה וְהִלָּ֥חֶם בּֽוֹ

verses.restored: Gaal went out before lords of Shechem and fought with Abimelech.

familiar.text: And Gaal went out before the men of Shechem, and fought with Abimelech.

modern.text: So Gaal went out before the leaders of Shechem and fought against Abimelech,

original.text: וַיֵּ֣צֵא גַ֔עַל לִפְנֵ֖י בַּעֲלֵ֣י שְׁכֶ֑ם וַיִּלָּ֖חֶם בַּאֲבִימֶֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: Abimelech pursued him, and he fled before him; many fell slain as far as entrance of gate.

familiar.text: And Abimelech chased him, and he fled before him, and many were overthrown and wounded, even unto the entering of the gate.

modern.text: but Abimelech pursued him, and Gaal fled before him. And many Shechemites fell wounded all the way to the entrance of the gate.

original.text: וַיִּרְדְּפֵ֣הוּ אֲבִימֶ֔לֶךְ וַיָּ֖נָס מִפָּנָ֑יו וַֽיִּפְּל֛וּ חֲלָלִ֥ים רַבִּ֖ים עַד פֶּ֥תַח הַשָּֽׁעַר

verses.restored: Abimelech dwelt at Arumah, and Zebul drove out Gaal and his brothers from dwelling in Shechem.

familiar.text: And Abimelech dwelt at Arumah: and Zebul thrust out Gaal and his brethren, that they should not dwell in Shechem.

modern.text: Abimelech stayed in Arumah, and Zebul drove Gaal and his brothers out of Shechem.

original.text: וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב אֲבִימֶ֖לֶךְ בָּארוּמָ֑ה וַיְגָ֧רֶשׁ זְבֻ֛ל אֶת גַּ֥עַל וְאֶת אֶחָ֖יו מִשֶּׁ֥בֶת בִּשְׁכֶֽם

verses.restored: It was next day that people went out to field, and they told Abimelech.

familiar.text: And it came to pass on the morrow, that the people went out into the field; and they told Abimelech.

modern.text: The next day the people of Shechem went out into the fields, and this was reported to Abimelech.

original.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ מִֽמָּחֳרָ֔ת וַיֵּצֵ֥א הָעָ֖ם הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה וַיַּגִּ֖דוּ לַאֲבִימֶֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: He took people, divided them into three companies, and lay in ambush in field. He looked, and behold, people were coming out from city; he rose against them and struck them.

familiar.text: And he took the people, and divided them into three companies, and laid wait in the field, and looked, and, behold, the people were come forth out of the city; and he rose up against them, and smote them.

modern.text: So he took his men, divided them into three companies, and lay in wait in the fields. When he saw the people coming out of the city, he rose up against them and attacked them.

original.text: וַיִּקַּ֣ח אֶת הָעָ֗ם וַֽיֶּחֱצֵם֙ לִשְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה רָאשִׁ֔ים וַיֶּאֱרֹ֖ב בַּשָּׂדֶ֑ה וַיַּ֗רְא וְהִנֵּ֤ה הָעָם֙ יֹצֵ֣א מִן הָעִ֔יר וַיָּ֥קָם עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם וַיַּכֵּֽם

verses.restored: Abimelech and companies with him rushed and stood at entrance of gate of city, while two companies rushed upon all who were in field and struck them.

familiar.text: And Abimelech, and the company that was with him, rushed forward, and stood in the entering of the gate of the city: and the two other companies ran upon all the people that were in the fields, and slew them.

modern.text: Then Abimelech and the companies with him rushed forward and took their stand at the entrance of the city gate. The other two companies rushed against all who were in the fields and struck them down.

original.text: וַאֲבִימֶ֗לֶךְ וְהָרָאשִׁים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עִמּ֔וֹ פָּשְׁט֕וּ וַיַּ֣עַמְד֔וּ פֶּ֖תַח שַׁ֣עַר הָעִ֑יר וּשְׁנֵ֣י הָֽרָאשִׁ֗ים פָּֽשְׁט֛וּ עַֽל כָּל אֲשֶׁ֥ר בַּשָּׂדֶ֖ה וַיַּכּֽוּם

verses.restored: Abimelech fought against city all that day, captured city, killed people in it, tore down city, and sowed it with salt.

familiar.text: And Abimelech fought against the city all that day; and he took the city, and slew the people that was therein, and beat down the city, and sowed it with salt.

modern.text: And all that day Abimelech fought against the city until he had captured it and killed its people. Then he demolished the city and sowed it with salt.

original.text: וַאֲבִימֶ֜לֶךְ נִלְחָ֣ם בָּעִ֗יר כֹּ֚ל הַיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא וַיִּלְכֹּד֙ אֶת הָעִ֔יר וְאֶת הָעָ֥ם אֲשֶׁר בָּ֖הּ הָרָ֑ג וַיִּתֹּץ֙ אֶת הָעִ֔יר וַיִּזְרָעֶ֖הָ מֶֽלַח

verses.restored: All lords of tower of Shechem heard and entered stronghold of house of El-berith.

familiar.text: And when all the men of the tower of Shechem heard that, they entered into an hold of the house of the god Berith.

modern.text: On hearing of this, all the leaders in the tower of Shechem entered the inner chamber of the temple of El-berith.

original.text: וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֔וּ כָּֽל בַּעֲלֵ֖י מִֽגְדַּל שְׁכֶ֑ם וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ אֶל צְרִ֔יחַ בֵּ֖ית אֵ֥ל בְּרִֽית

verses.restored: It was told to Abimelech that all lords of tower of Shechem had gathered.

familiar.text: And it was told Abimelech, that all the men of the tower of Shechem were gathered together.

modern.text: And when Abimelech was told that all the leaders in the tower of Shechem were gathered there,

original.text: וַיֻּגַּ֖ד לַאֲבִימֶ֑לֶךְ כִּ֣י הִֽתְקַבְּצ֔וּ כָּֽל בַּעֲלֵ֖י מִֽגְדַּל שְׁכֶֽם

verses.restored: Abimelech went up to Mount Zalmon, he and all people with him. Abimelech took axes in his hand, cut down a branch of trees, lifted it, put it on his shoulder, and said to people with him, What you have seen me do, hurry, do as I have done.

familiar.text: And Abimelech gat him up to mount Zalmon, he and all the people that were with him; and Abimelech took an axe in his hand, and cut down a bough from the trees, and took it, and laid it on his shoulder, and said unto the people that were with him, What ye have seen me do, make haste, and do as I have done.

modern.text: he and all his men went up to Mount Zalmon. Abimelech took his axe in his hand and cut a branch from the trees, which he lifted to his shoulder, saying to his men, “Hurry and do what you have seen me do.”

original.text: וַיַּ֨עַל אֲבִימֶ֜לֶךְ הַר צַלְמ֗וֹן הוּא֮ וְכָל הָעָ֣ם אֲשֶׁר אִתּוֹ֒ וַיִּקַּח֩ אֲבִימֶ֨לֶךְ אֶת הַקַּרְדֻּמּ֜וֹת בְּיָד֗וֹ וַיִּכְרֹת֙ שׂוֹכַ֣ת עֵצִ֔ים וַיִּ֨שָּׂאֶ֔הָ וַיָּ֖שֶׂם עַל שִׁכְמ֑וֹ וַיֹּ֜אמֶר אֶל הָעָ֣ם אֲשֶׁר עִמּ֗וֹ מָ֤ה רְאִיתֶם֙ עָשִׂ֔יתִי מַהֲר֖וּ עֲשׂ֥וּ כָמֽוֹנִי

verses.restored: All people also cut each man his branch and went after Abimelech, set them against stronghold, and set stronghold on fire over them. All people of tower of Shechem also died, about a thousand men and women.

familiar.text: And all the people likewise cut down every man his bough, and followed Abimelech, and put them to the hold, and set the hold on fire upon them; so that all the men of the tower of Shechem died also, about a thousand men and women.

modern.text: So each man also cut his own branch and followed Abimelech. Then they piled the branches against the inner chamber and set it on fire above them, killing everyone in the tower of Shechem, about a thousand men and women. Abimelech’s Punishment

modern.text: Then Abimelech went to Thebez, encamped against it, and captured it.

verses.restored: A strong tower was in midst of city, and there fled all men and women and all lords of city. They shut themselves in and went up on roof of tower.

familiar.text: But there was a strong tower within the city, and thither fled all the men and women, and all they of the city, and shut it to them, and gat them up to the top of the tower.

modern.text: But there was a strong tower inside the city, and all the men, women, and leaders of the city fled there. They locked themselves in and went up to the roof of the tower.

modern.text: When Abimelech came to attack the tower, he approached its entrance to set it on fire.

verses.restored: He called quickly to young man, his armor-bearer, and said to him, Draw your sword and kill me, lest they say of me, A woman killed him. His young man thrust him through, and he died.

familiar.text: Then he called hastily unto the young man his armourbearer, and said unto him, Draw thy sword, and slay me, that men say not of me, A woman slew him. And his young man thrust him through, and he died.

modern.text: He quickly called his armor-bearer, saying, “Draw your sword and kill me, lest they say of me, ‘A woman killed him.’” So Abimelech’s armor-bearer ran his sword through him, and he died.

familiar.text: And when the men of Israel saw that Abimelech was dead, they departed every man unto his place.

modern.text: And when the Israelites saw that Abimelech was dead, they all went home.

modern.text: In this way God repaid the wickedness that Abimelech had done to his father in murdering his seventy brothers.

modern.text: And God also brought all the wickedness of the men of Shechem back upon their own heads. So the curse of Jotham son of Jerubbaal came upon them.

translation_notes: Abimelech builds power through kinship manipulation, temple funds, hired reckless men, and mass fratricide. This is anti-kingship narrative, not a legitimate accession story.
The phrase 'son of his slave woman' exposes status hierarchy and maternal shaming in Jotham's speech; the critique of Abimelech must not become contempt for enslaved or secondary-status mothers.
Jotham's fable contrasts fruitful trees that refuse domination with bramble kingship that offers false shade and real fire.
The evil spirit between Abimelech and Shechem describes destructive rupture and mutual treachery; it must not be weaponized against mentally ill or neurodivergent people.
Abimelech's violence escalates from brother-killing to civil terror, city destruction, salt-sowing, and burning a thousand men and women inside a tower.
The woman of Thebez kills Abimelech with an upper millstone, reversing his attempt to burn another tower full of civilians.
Abimelech's fear of being remembered as killed by a woman exposes misogynistic honor anxiety, not a valid shame.
The final verses frame the chapter as bloodguilt returning upon Abimelech and Shechem, but this should not justify cycles of revenge or civilian massacre.
safety_note: Do not use Judges 9 to justify monarchy by violence, family slaughter, mercenary politics, collective burning, ableist evil-spirit language, maternal-status shaming, misogynistic honor codes, or revenge cycles. Center Jotham's anti-tyrant warning: bramble power promises shade and produces fire.
